provider.notes: The plugin registry's canonical id is microsoft-azure with alias azure (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:92-98, :1677-1680); the live speech-to-text name tables accept only those two spellings (gateway/src/plugin/dispatch.rs:257 and :280; gateway/src/core/stt/mod.rs:400). microsoft_azure is accepted only by a vendor-name helper on the REST audio routes (gateway/src/handlers/openai_audio.rs:1503-1505); a live session using that spelling would be refused today as an unknown provider (gateway/src/plugin/registry.rs:310-320; inferred from reading, not run), so it is listed as an alias for the resolver to normalise, not because it works today. The standardized factory matches only the spelling 'azure' (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:412), so a session naming microsoft-azure falls to the flat factory (:476) and loses region, api_base and every standardized feature; the resolver must normalise the provider id before lookup. The reach of that split is narrower than it looks: a Bud voice-agent leg copies the deployment's vendor string into the session (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:223), and Bud publishes Azure Speech under the vendor name azure (comment at gateway/src/core/tts/self_hosted.rs:108-109), so Bud legs reach the standardized factory and only sessions that name microsoft-azure take the flat one. Azure Speech real-time recognition has no model id on the wire, so the model string is a name the gateway defines, and today's client never reads it (gateway/src/core/stt/azure/config.rs:552, :670), so the capability lookup must run before the client is built. Sessions are expected to reach this provider with model ids other than 'default' (inferred from two things read in the repository): the gateway's own documentation tells customers to put a Custom Speech endpoint id in the model field (gateway/docs/azure-stt.md:76, :183-191), and a Bud deployment's stored model string is copied into the session (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:223-226; a comment at gateway/src/core/tts/self_hosted.rs:108 says Bud publishes Azure Speech models under names of the form azure/speech/..., the exact speech-to-text strings were not confirmed). Every such id resolves to the provider default row, so that row decides the path of those sessions. 'llm-speech' is a proposed gateway sentinel for the LLM Speech product, which has no vendor model string. Not listed as transports: batch transcription and Whisper inside Azure Speech (asynchronous jobs that can take up to 30 minutes to start) and the 60-second short-audio REST call (Microsoft positions it as a last resort). Azure OpenAI audio models (whisper, gpt-transcribe, the gpt-4o transcribe family, gpt-live-transcribe, gpt-realtime-whisper) belong to the separate provider id azure_openai (rows/azure_openai.json), not to this file.

gateway_client.notes: Exercised only against an in-repo mock server. Microsoft documents the Speech SDK, not the raw socket frames, so the client's framing is an inferred contract. The client ignores the model id. Known risks: a BabbleTimeout status ends the stream as fatal (messages.rs:82-84, client.rs:562-570); turn.end is only logged (client.rs:590-592); the sample rate header copies the session rate with no WAV header (client.rs:458-463) although Microsoft documents only 16 kHz and 8 kHz. The 100 concurrent requests limit is the S0 tier default per Speech resource (1 on the free tier).
